title: Hot Dry Noodles (Wuhan Sesame Noodles)
summary: Wuhan-style hot dry noodles: springy wheat noodles tossed with a rich sesame sauce, tangy black vinegar, pickled mustard stem and a spoonful of chilli oil.

ingredients.item: fresh alkaline wheat noodles (or 300 g dried ramen-style noodles)
garlic cloves, crushed to a paste and mixed with 3 tbsp water
preserved mustard stem (zha cai) or pickled radish, finely chopped

steps.title: Par-cook the noodles
steps.text: Boil the noodles for 1-2 minutes less than the packet time, so they're still slightly firm in the centre. This undercooking matters because the noodles will be reheated briefly later, and starting too soft leaves them mushy by the time they're served.

steps.title: Cool and oil the noodles
steps.text: Drain the noodles and immediately toss them with the 3 tsp of sesame oil, then spread them out on the tray, lifting and turning them as they cool, using a fan if you have one. Cooling them quickly while coated in oil is what gives hot dry noodles their characteristic springy, separate strands rather than a sticky clump.

steps.title: Loosen the sesame paste
steps.text: Stir the sesame paste with the sesame oil, then beat in the warm water a spoonful at a time until the mixture pours like thick cream. Adding the water gradually stops the thick paste seizing into a stiff, unworkable lump.

steps.title: Reheat the noodles
steps.text: Bring a pot of water back to the boil, then dip portions of the cooled noodles in a sieve for 20-30 seconds just to warm them through. This brief reheat brings the noodles back to serving temperature without softening them past their springy bite.

steps.title: Assemble and dress
steps.text: Divide the warm noodles among bowls and top each with the light and dark soy sauces, vinegar, sugar, white pepper, garlic water, a generous spoonful of the sesame sauce, zha cai and spring onions, finishing with chilli oil. Layering the seasonings on top rather than mixing them in beforehand means each bowl can be stirred fresh at the table.

steps.title: Mix thoroughly before eating
steps.text: Toss everything together at the table until every strand of noodle is evenly coated in sauce. A thorough mix is essential here, since the dish has no broth to carry the flavour otherwise.

tips: Undercook the noodles slightly at the first boil — they get a second brief dip in hot water later, and fully cooked noodles will turn soft and gluey by serving time.
Loosen the sesame paste with water gradually; tipping it all in at once can make the paste clump and separate instead of turning smooth.
Toss thoroughly and immediately once the toppings are added, as hot dry noodles rely on the mix-in at the table rather than a pre-made sauce.
Don't skip cooling the noodles with the fan or by spreading them out — noodles left to cool in a pile will stick together in clumps.
storage: The dressed noodles are meant to be eaten straight away, as they lose their spring and turn claggy once dressed and left standing. Cooked, undressed noodles can be kept in the fridge for up to 1 day; reheat with the brief hot-water dip described above rather than in a microwave. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
